title: feat(ci): polish release notes for a range of releases
body: The **Polish release notes** workflow can now rewrite a batch of releases in one run. ## Usage Actions → Polish release notes → Run workflow: - `tag`: the newest release, e.g. `v2.6.2` - `from_tag` (new, optional): the oldest release, e.g. `v2.5.0`. Every published release from it through `tag` is rewritten. Leave it empty to rewrite only `tag`, as before. - `dry_run` works as before and applies to every release in the range. ## How it works - A new `releases` job lists the published releases (no drafts), sorts them by version, and takes the inclusive range. It fails if either tag isn't a published release, if `from_tag` is newer than `tag`, or if the range has more than 256 releases (the matrix limit). - `polish` runs once per release as a matrix job: - `fail-fast: false`, so one bad release doesn't stop the rest. - `max-parallel: 3`, to stay within the Azure OpenAI rate limit. - The per-tag concurrency group moved from the workflow to the job, so two runs never edit the same release at once. - The polish script is unchanged. A release that was already polished is rewritten again from the original notes it stores. - On the release-published event, `releases` outputs just that release's tag. ## Testing - Ran the range script against this repo's real releases: - `v2.5.0` → `v2.6.2` gives `v2.5.0` through `v2.6.2` (7 releases). - An empty `from_tag` gives `v2.6.2` alone. - A reversed range and an unknown tag each fail with a clear message. - The YAML parses. The workflow itself hasn't run yet. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic The Polish release notes workflow can now rewrite a batch of releases in one run. - A new optional `from_tag` input rewrites every published release from it through `tag`; leaving it empty keeps the old single-tag behavior. - Each release in the range runs as its own matrix job, 3 at a time, with per-tag concurrency so runs never edit the same release at once; one failure doesn't stop the rest. - The range lists every published release across all API pages and sorts pre-releases before their final release (e.g. `v2.6.2-rc.1` before `v2.6.2`). - The workflow fails with a clear error if a tag isn't a published release, the range is reversed, or the range exceeds 256 releases. - The polish script is unchanged; already-polished releases are rewritten from the original notes they store. title: fix(helm): set fsGroup so the persistence PVC is writable
body: ## Summary With `persistence.enabled: true`, the browser pod fails to start because the mounted PVC is not writable. ## Root cause The image runs as the non-root `nextjs` user (uid/gid 1001, see `Dockerfile`). Freshly provisioned PVCs are typically owned by `root:root`. Since the container is not root, `docker-entrypoint.sh` cannot chown `/app/.data`, its write check fails, and the pod exits. The chart's `podSecurityContext` set `runAsUser`/`runAsGroup` but no `fsGroup`. This is the same class of bug fixed in DM-SQL-to-FalkorDB v1.1.9 (FalkorDB/DM-SQL-to-FalkorDB#58), whose description notes the browser chart is affected too. ## Fix - `values.yaml`: add `podSecurityContext.fsGroup: 1001` and `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` (avoids a recursive re-own on every restart). Both are overridable. - `README.md`: update the `podSecurityContext` parameter row. - `Chart.yaml`: bump chart version 1.7.0 → 1.7.1 (`appVersion` unchanged; no image change). ## Testing - `values.yaml` parses and the new keys are present. - Not yet run: `helm lint` / `helm template` and an install with `persistence.enabled=true` (helm/docker unavailable in the authoring environment). Please verify in CI or on a cluster. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Makes the persistence volume writable when `persistence.enabled` is set, fixing a startup failure where the browser pod could not write to a root-owned PVC because the container runs as the non-root `nextjs` user. - Adds `fsGroup: 1001` and `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` to the chart's default `podSecurityContext`, both overridable. - Documents the new defaults in `README.md` and bumps the chart version to 1.7.1. Written for commit de06caf767eb45402d85e7694b5ce7ccff9d344f. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Updated the default pod security settings so non-root containers can write to newly provisioned persistence volumes. Volume ownership is adjusted only when needed. * **Documentation** * Updated the chart documentation to reflect the default volume access and security settings.

title: feat: desktop and mobile apps, with an OS-aware "Get the app" in the browser
body: ## Summary Ships FalkorDB Browser as a **desktop app** (Electron: Windows, macOS, Linux) and a **mobile app** (Capacitor: Android, plus iOS through Add to Home Screen for now). The web browser now offers each visitor the app for their OS. Nothing changes for the existing web, Docker, Helm or Vercel deployments. ### Desktop (`desktop/`) - Runs the same standalone `server.js` the Docker image runs, on `127.0.0.1`, and opens a window on it. Each install generates and keeps its own `AUTH_SECRET` / `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (`secrets.json`, mode 600), and stores API tokens and CSV temp files in the OS app-data folder. - `.next/standalone` can contain a developer's `.env*`, `.data/` (API tokens) and other local folders; these never ship (`pruneServer`). - Publishing a GitHub release builds the installers on each OS and attaches them under fixed names, e.g. `FalkorDB-Browser-win-x64.exe`. The fixed names keep `releases/latest/download/…` links stable. ### Mobile (`mobile/`) - A Capacitor shell that opens one deployment of the browser. `capacitor.config.ts` accepts only `https://`; plain http requires `FALKORDB_BROWSER_ALLOW_HTTP=1`, which only `npm run dev:android` sets, and the cleartext permission goes in the debug manifest only. - `mobile/aws/`: a CloudFormation template that runs the published image on ECS Fargate behind an HTTPS ALB. App Runner no longer accepts new customers. - Publishing a release builds a signed APK (`FalkorDB-Browser-android.apk`) once the signing secrets exist. Without them the job logs a warning and the release goes out without it. ### "Get the app" in the browser - A popup on whichever page the visitor lands on, including `/graph` for users with a saved session, plus a link on the login page and in the menus. It shows once per session, stops after "Don't show this again" or a download, waits for the tutorial to close, and never shows inside the desktop or mobile app or after a Home Screen launch. - Desktop visitors get the latest installer for their OS. Phone links come from `ANDROID_APP_URL` / `IOS_APP_URL` (`/api/app-links`). A phone app opens only the server it was built for, so these are opt-in per deployment. iOS falls back to Add to Home Screen, which now opens full screen with its own icon. ### Fix found along the way Radix's scroll lock reset the body's safe-area padding to 0. On an edge-to-edge screen (the Android app, or iOS from the Home Screen), opening any menu therefore shifted the page up under the status bar. A CSS rule now keeps the padding while scroll is locked. ## Not in this PR (by choice) Code signing and store publishing: Apple notarization, Windows signing, Google Play. Until those are set up, macOS and Windows show their usual warnings for unsigned downloads, and Android shows its warning for installing apps from outside a store. The workflows already accept the credentials as secrets, so adding them later needs no code change. ## Existing workflows - **CI:** `nextjs.yml`, `playwright.yml`, `release-image.yml`, `helm-chart.yml`, `daily-security-scan.yml` and `drift-canary.yml` are untouched. - **New workflows:** `desktop.yml` and `mobile.yml` run only on changes under `desktop/` or `mobile/`, on manual dispatch, and when a release is published. - **Root config:** `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs` and `.dockerignore` now exclude `desktop/` and `mobile/`. - **E2E suites:** every suite seeds `appDownloadPrompt=false` next to `tutorial=false` (`initializeLocalStorage`), so the popup never covers what an existing test clicks. ## Tests - **Unit** (`lib/appDownload.test.ts`, 100% coverage, added to `test:coverage`): OS detection, which download each platform gets, the http opt-in for app links, the session and dismissal rules, and unavailable storage. - **E2E** (`e2e/tests/appDownload.spec.ts`, 15 tests, plus one in `tutorialWalkthrough.spec.ts`): - the installer per desktop OS on `/graph` - once per session, "don't show again", download dismissal - the login page and the help and mobile menus - Android with and without a link - iOS: Home Screen steps, an App Store link, and a Home Screen launch - no popup inside the desktop or mobile app - the popup waits for the tutorial - **Desktop** (`desktop/test`, 11 tests, run on all 3 OSes in CI): secrets persistence and permissions, port reuse and fallback, the server's environment, which URLs stay in the window, the external-link allowlist, the prune list, and resource paths. - **Mobile** (`mobile/test`, 7 tests): the config's URL rules, and the release version stamping (`v2.6.1` → versionCode `20601`), which refuses tags that aren't `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Verified locally: - lint, `tsc`, `test:coverage` (688 passing) and `next build` - a packaged Linux AppImage serving pages - a signed release APK, checked with `apksigner` - the e2e suite against an isolated FalkorDB Two tutorial e2e tests, "walk through the entire tutorial" and "clicking away", fail locally on clean `staging` as well (local FalkorDB 4.18.3), so they aren't caused by this change. The macOS and Windows installers have only been built by this PR's CI run. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Ships FalkorDB Browser as an Electron desktop app and a Capacitor mobile app, and offers each web visitor the app for their OS. The existing web, Docker, Helm, and Vercel deployments are unchanged. The desktop shell runs the same standalone `server.js` the Docker image runs, on `127.0.0.1`, keeping its own secrets and app data in the OS app-data folder. Publishing a GitHub release builds installers for Windows, Linux, Apple silicon, and Intel macOS under fixed names so `releases/latest/download` links stay stable; a macOS relaunch waits for the server before opening its window. The mobile side is a Capacitor shell that opens one HTTPS deployment; a CloudFormation template runs the published image on ECS Fargate behind an HTTPS ALB. Its `deploy.sh` creates secrets only for a new stack, keeps them across updates, can store API tokens in FalkorDB via `API_TOKEN_FALKORDB_URL`, and stops unless the current token-store URL reads cleanly. Releases attach a signed Android APK when the signing secrets exist. An OS-aware "Get the app" popup shows once per session on the landing page (including `/graph` for saved sessions), waits for the loaded page, the tutorial, and the What's New popup so the two first-visit popups never overlap, and never appears inside the desktop or mobile app or after a Home Screen launch. Every e2e suite seeds `appDownloadPrompt=false`. title: feat(tabs): share by copying the address bar instead of a copy-link button
body:
## Problem
People share a graph by copying the address bar, but it only carried `?tab=<id>`, a key into the sender's localStorage. The pasted link opened nothing for anyone else. The real share action was a 12px "Copy link" icon between the rename and close buttons, and people didn't notice it.

## Change
- The address bar now carries the active tab's portable state (`graph`, `query`, `view`, `layout`, `direction`) next to `tab`, so a copied URL opens for anyone.
- On entry, a `tab` id that exists in the visitor's own storage still wins, so reloads are unchanged. An unknown id, or one naming a blank tab, falls back to opening the params as a shared tab (`resolveEntryTabs` in `lib/graphTabs.ts`).
- Layout and direction come from the live canvas (graph and schema views), not the tab's stored copy, so the address bar follows layout changes right away. A tab without a graph puts no share params on the URL.
- The URL sync waits 300ms after the last change, because the query changes on every keystroke and Safari throws if `replaceState` is called too often.
- The Copy link button (desktop and mobile), `shareUrl`, `buildShareUrl` and their page-object helpers are removed.

## Notes
- Queries now always appear in the address bar and browser history, not only in shared links.

## Tests
- Unit: `shareParams`, `withLiveLayout`, `resolveEntryTabs` and `buildGraphUrlParams` share params. `graphTabs.ts` and `urlParams.ts` stay at 100% coverage.
- E2E (`graphTabs.spec.ts`, 16/16 on Chromium and Firefox): a URL copied out of the address bar opens in a clean browser; a reload keeps the user's tab over stale URL params; a blank tab puts no graph on the URL. The two clipboard tests for the removed button are dropped.

title: fix(tabs): a share link opens on a first visit instead of the tutorial
body:
Follow-up to #2116, which was merged just before this fix was pushed.

## Problem

A browser that has never opened the app starts the tutorial automatically. The tutorial swaps in a blank tab of its own and demo graphs, so the person a share link was sent to sees "New tab" and an empty canvas instead of the shared graph. The link only opens once they dismiss the tour.

title: feat(tabs): shareable links that open a tab's graph and query anywhere
body:
## Problem

Since the tab strip landed, the `/graph` URL only carries `?tab=<id>`. That id is looked up in the visitor's own connection-scoped localStorage, so a link sent to anyone else (or opened in another browser or on another connection) quietly opens whatever that person had open last.

## Approach

The two jobs are now handled separately:

- **`?tab=<id>`** stays as it is: it points at your own tab, so a reload lands where you left off.
- **Share link**: built only when you click, from a new per-tab "Copy link" button (desktop strip and mobile menu). It carries only what means the same thing on another machine:
  `/graph?graph=…&query=…&view=…&layout=…&direction=…`
  Viewport, selection, panel/chat state and the tab id are left out.

Because the link is built on click rather than kept in the address bar, it doesn't change when you keep working in the tab, and the URL isn't rewritten on every pan or zoom.

### Opening a link
- If a tab with the same graph and query already exists, it is selected, so opening your own link doesn't create a duplicate.
- Otherwise the link opens in a new active tab. This is allowed even at the tab limit, because the user asked for it and the strip already handles going over the limit.
- The rebuild runs through the existing `handleActivateTab` path. The query is **always read-only**, and a graph that doesn't exist on the recipient's server is never queried, so a link can't write data or create a graph.
- After it opens, the URL sync removes the share params and the address bar goes back to `?tab=<id>`.
- The link is read when the page first renders, so it survives a signed-out visitor's client-side redirect to `/login` and back.

## Changes
- `lib/graphTabs.ts`: adds `SHARE_PARAM_KEYS`, `buildShareUrl`, `parseSharedTab` and `withSharedTab` (pure functions, unit-tested).
- `lib/useGraphTabs.ts`: restore takes `initialShare`, and the hook exposes `shareUrl(id)`, which includes the active tab's current layout.
- `lib/urlParams.ts`: the `/graph` builder removes the share params.
- `app/providers.tsx`: reads the share link from the URL on the first render.
- `app/graph/GraphSubHeader.tsx`: the copy-link button, plus a toast saying whether the copy worked.

## Testing
- [x] `npm test`: 604 passed, including new tests for building, parsing, reusing an existing tab, the schema view's layout, the tab limit, the URL cleanup and `createTab`.
- [x] `npm run test:coverage`: `lib/graphTabs.ts` and `lib/urlParams.ts` are now in the 100% line/branch/function gate, and both are at 100%.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and eslint reports no new warnings.
- [ ] e2e (`e2e/tests/graphTabs.spec.ts`, 5 new tests): a link opens and clears itself, your own link reuses your tab, a blank tab can't be shared, the copy button's link opens the same context in a fresh browser, and a failed copy shows an error. The clipboard is stubbed so these also run on Firefox. **Not run locally**: no FalkorDB instance was available, so these need to be checked in CI.

## Known gaps / follow-ups
- If the shared graph doesn't exist on the recipient's server, the tab opens with no graph and keeps the query text, with no message. A "graph not found" toast would help.
- A full page reload on `/login` loses a pending link. Saving it in `sessionStorage` would cover that.

body:
Fixes #1084

**Also in this PR (from #2123):** the e2e regression test for #1084, `@admin Every node stays hoverable and clickable when canvas pixel reads are scrambled`. It goes with `simulateCanvasFingerprintNoise()` in `e2e/infra/utils.ts`, which flips low bits of single-pixel `getImageData` reads the way Brave's fingerprinting protection does. The fix itself is `@falkordb/canvas` 0.2.9, already required here. The test passes in `[Admin] Chromium` and `[Admin] Firefox`, as does the whole of `canvas.spec.ts` (65/65).

Sources ten shared primitives from `@falkordb/ui` instead of keeping a local
copy of each, and fixes three mobile layout bugs found while proving the
migration changes nothing visible.

Pairs with FalkorDB/falkordb-ui#11.

## What changed

**Migrated to the design system** — badge, card, checkbox, dialog, select,
switch, textarea, tooltip, plus the app's `Button` and `Input`. Each wrapper now
holds only what the browser does differently, with a comment saying why; 490
lines of duplicated primitive deleted against 232 added. `Input` is a
re-export. `Button` keeps its `Primary` / `Secondary` / `Cancel` / `Delete` /
`button` names as a small map onto the design system's variants, so no call site
changes, and keeps the long-press touch tooltip.

**Mobile fixes**

- The Create New Graph dialog no longer spills off a phone screen. An input will
  not shrink below its intrinsic width, so the name row was 363px of content in
  a 282px dialog; it now wraps and the input takes a line of its own. The footer
  buttons need 323px side by side and `justify-end` pushed the overflow off the
  *left* edge, cutting the confirm button in half — they wrap too.
- The canvas toolbar actions are grouped and ordered the way mobile already
  does it, rather than reversed and pinned to the right edge, and Show All now
  collapses together with Search & Filter instead of being left behind.

## Verification

`tsc`, ESLint (0 errors), 590 unit tests and the production build are all clean.

The migration was checked against staging rather than by eye. Every element on
nine screens at phone width was fingerprinted — width, height, padding, font
size, radius, border, colours, display, gap, z-index, min-height, min-width,
weight and shadow — with this branch's primitives and then with staging's. 630
elements compared, no differences. Desktop was measured the same way before and
after the dialog fix, which is entirely behind the `mobile:` variant.

## Follow-up

`@falkordb/ui` is pinned to a branch here. Once FalkorDB/falkordb-ui#10 and #11
land and `0.2.0` is published, the dependency becomes `^0.2.0`.

`npm ci` currently reports `Missing: openapi-types@12.1.3 from lock file`. That
reproduces identically on `staging` with the same npm, so it is pre-existing and
not from this branch.

title: feat(auth): support a preconfigured connection that signs in automatically
body:
Closes #1896 (partially — single connection, see "Scope" below).

## Why

A GitOps deployment of the browser has nobody to type credentials into the login form. Issue #1896 asks for connections to be declared in Helm values so a cluster can ship the browser already pointed at its database.

## Scope

This is the **single-connection** slice of the issue: one operator-supplied connection that the browser is already signed into when it loads. The multi-connection array (`connections.items`) is not implemented.

## How it works

The connection is read from the environment:

| Variable | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FALKORDB_CONNECTION_URL` | `falkor://`, `falkors://`, `redis://` or `rediss://` URL; the `s` variants imply TLS | `""` |
| `FALKORDB_HOST` | Hostname. Required unless the URL is set | `""` |
| `FALKORDB_PORT` | Port | `6379` |
| `FALKORDB_USERNAME` | Username | `default` |
| `FALKORDB_PASSWORD` | Password | `""` |
| `FALKORDB_TLS` | `true`/`false`; overrides the URL scheme | from the URL |
| `FALKORDB_CA` | Base64-encoded CA certificate | `""` |
| `FALKORDB_AUTO_CONNECT` | Sign in automatically on load. `false` only prefills the login form | `true` |

The discrete fields override the URL **field by field**, so an empty `FALKORDB_PASSWORD` also overrides it — the Helm templates therefore omit empty values rather than emitting `""`. Malformed input throws at read time rather than being guessed at.

The Helm chart exposes the same settings under `connection.*`, with an `existingSecret` variant for the URL, password and CA.

## Security

- **The password never crosses the wire.** The client posts `preconfigured: "true"` to the credentials provider and `authorize()` replaces *every* field with the server-side value, so a client cannot influence which database it authenticates against.
- The discovery endpoint `GET /api/connections/preconfigured` is deliberately unauthenticated, because the login page consults it before there is a session. It returns the host, port, username and TLS flag only — never the password or the CA.
- With auto-connect enabled, anyone who can reach the browser reaches the database with these credentials. That trade-off is called out in `values.yaml`, `.env.local.template` and both READMEs, with a recommendation to use a read-only FalkorDB user.

## Sign-out

title: fix(tutorial): drop leftover demo graphs before re-creating them
body:
Fixes #2087

## The bug

The tutorial loads its demo data with a plain `CREATE`, which only ever appends:

```ts
getSSEGraphResult(`/api/graph/social-demo?query=${prepareArg(socialQuery)}`, ...)
```

Nothing checks whether the graph is already there. The only guard was the `demoLoaded` state in `Tutorial.tsx`, which resets on unmount.

Two things make that compound without bound:

- the tutorial **re-opens by itself on every page load** until it is dismissed (`setTutorialOpen(localStorage.getItem("tutorial") !== "false")`);
- the cleanup that drops the demo graphs runs **only** when the tutorial is finished or closed — a refresh or a closed tab skips it.

So every reload stacks another full copy on top of the old one. The reporter's `social-demo` reached 7,875 `:Person` nodes with 9 distinct names — 875 copies.

Reproduced against a live FalkorDB: two runs of the demo `CREATE` give 4 nodes where the dataset has 2; `DELETE` first and it stays at 2.

## The fix

Delete both demo graphs before creating them, so the load is idempotent however the previous session ended.

The delete is **unconditional** rather than gated on the graph list. `handleFetchOptions` early-returns while the tutorial is open, so `graphNames` is `undefined` in exactly the reload case that causes the duplication — a `graphNames.includes(...)` guard would skip the clean-up precisely when it is needed. Deleting a graph that does not exist answers 400 (`ERR Invalid graph operation on empty key`), which is the normal first-run case, so the pre-clean passes a no-op toast instead of raising a destructive toast at every first-time user. A genuinely failing delete is therefore silent, which is the right trade: a toast there would fire for everyone and tell them nothing actionable.

Two smaller things fell out of it:

- leftover demo names are filtered out of `userGraphsBeforeTutorial`, so a previous session's `social-demo` is not restored into the selector as a ghost entry after cleanup;
- the three copies of the delete pair are folded into one `DEMO_GRAPH_NAMES` constant.

## Not done, deliberately

A user's own graph literally named `social-demo` is still clobbered. That is pre-existing — the tutorial cleanup already deleted it — so this is not a regression, and fixing it properly means namespacing the demo graphs, which changes every tutorial step's copy.

## Test

`e2e/tests/tutorialWalkthrough.spec.ts` gains a regression test: open the tutorial, count `:Person` in `social-demo`, refresh mid-tutorial (which skips the cleanup and re-auto-opens the tutorial), count again. On `staging` the second count is 18; with this change it stays 9.

title: fix(cypher): parse LOAD CSV and VECTOR INDEX, and catch unrunnable CSV sources
body:
Fixes #2056 and #2058, plus the pre-flight layer they made necessary.

## The two grammar bugs

Both issues are the same shape: valid FalkorDB Cypher that the bundled grammar did not know about, so the editor marked it as a syntax error and disabled **Run** — the query could not even be attempted.

| | Missing from the grammar |
|---|---|
| #2056 | `LOAD CSV [WITH HEADERS] FROM <uri> AS <var> [FIELDTERMINATOR '<c>']` — the clause did not exist at all |
| #2058 | No `VECTOR` token, and no index statement accepted a trailing `OPTIONS { … }` map |

Both are now in `Cypher.g4`. The seven new keywords (`LOAD`, `CSV`, `HEADERS`, `FROM`, `FIELDTERMINATOR`, `VECTOR`, `OPTIONS`) are also listed as non-reserved, so `RETURN 1 AS from` and `n.options` keep working.

The parser is regenerated with the `generate:grammar` npm script that `lib/falkordb-cypher/generated/README.md` already documented but which had never actually been committed — it and its `antlr4ng-cli` devDependency are now in the repo, so the next person does not have to rediscover the toolchain.

## Why a pre-flight check comes with it

Fixing the grammar exposes the opposite problem. `LOAD CSV` now parses happily with a source FalkorDB will never fetch, and the only feedback is a bare `Unsupported URI` after a round-trip. Verified against a live instance:

```
LOAD CSV FROM 'http://example.com/a.csv'  → Unsupported URI
LOAD CSV FROM 'ftp://example.com/a.csv'   → Unsupported URI
LOAD CSV FROM 'a.csv'                     → Unsupported URI
```

`lib/queryPreflight.ts` catches these at submit time. **It is deliberately not a syntax check**, and the distinction is the whole design:

- A *syntax* error means the text is malformed. It marks the query and disables Run.
- A *pre-flight* issue means the query is well-formed but certain to be rejected. **Run stays enabled** and the request is stopped in `handleSubmit`, which is exactly where we can still offer the fix: an **Upload CSV** button that opens the Load CSV tab, where the browser stores the file and fills in a URI FalkorDB can actually read.

The bar for adding a rule there is high — only deterministic, server-independent failures. A `$parameter` source, or a `file://` path that may or may not exist, is left to the server.

`file://` is the one scheme that gets no rule of its own by default. FalkorDB resolves it against its own `IMPORT_FOLDER`, so the question is really "does the database read files from the same place this browser writes them?" — and nothing the browser can see settles it. The CSV storage settings do not either: an instance can upload to S3 and still have a mounted import folder full of files a query may legitimately name. So only an operator saying `LOAD_CSV_FILE_URI=false` blocks it, and `/api/csv-temp/capabilities` serves that answer to the client. Everything else answers `true`, because the errors are not symmetrical: a wrong `true` just lets the query fail at the server as it does today, while a wrong `false` would block a query that works.

## Tests

- **`e2e/tests/queryPreflight.spec.ts`** (16 tests) — the grammar regressions live here because the generated parser cannot be loaded by `node --test`. Each "this is valid Cypher" case first types `MATCH (n) RETsURN n` and asserts a marker *does* appear, so a pass cannot come from the linter simply being asleep. Covers both `LOAD CSV` forms, `CREATE`/`DROP VECTOR INDEX … OPTIONS {…}`, the pre-flight block, the `$url` source that must be left alone, and clicking **Upload CSV** landing on the Load CSV tab.
- **`lib/queryPreflight.test.ts`** (13 tests) — every rejected scheme, the accepted ones, `LOAD CSV` hidden inside comments/strings/backticks, multi-clause queries, escaped literals, no regex state carryover.
- **`app/lib/csv-load-capabilities.test.ts`** (9 tests) — the override and its parsing, the default, and a negative control asserting the CSV storage configuration (including one broken enough to throw) is *not* read as a `false`.

Writing those turned up a bug: `isFileUriLoadSupported()` called `getResolvedCsvStorageMode()`, which *throws* on a misconfigured store (`CSV_STORAGE=s3` with no bucket), which would have 500'd the capabilities endpoint. It now fails open.

`npm test` (519) · `npm run build` · `tsc --noEmit` · `eslint app lib e2e` — all green.

title: fix(security): parameterise Cypher inputs, bind ciphertext to its owner, drop the baked AUTH_SECRET
body:
## What

Fixes seven findings from a security review, plus a toast overflow bug.

### Cypher injection

| Where | Problem |
| --- | --- |
| `app/api/graph/[graph]/[element]/label/route.ts` | A caller-supplied label went straight into `SET n:` / `REMOVE n:`. `Foo DETACH DELETE n //` wiped the graph. |
| `app/api/graph/[graph]/[element]/route.ts` | Same for labels, relationship types and attribute keys; attribute *values* were inlined as single-quoted strings. FalkorDB escapes a quote with `\'`, not `''`, so the doubling was bypassable. |
| `lib/token-storage/FalkorDBTokenStorage.ts` | All ten queries were built by concatenation behind a hand-rolled `escapeString` with the same `''` flaw — a personal access token **name** was an injection vector into the token graph. |
| `app/graph/graphInfo.tsx` | Three generated queries were quoted inconsistently. |

Identifiers now go through `quoteCypherIdentifier`; values are bound as parameters (`$attr_N`, `$nodeA`, `$nodeB`). `escapeString` is deleted and `executePATQuery` forwards params to `graph.query`.

`POST /api/graph/:graph/:element` also now returns an explicit `403` on a read-only connection instead of failing deeper in.

### Encryption

`/api/encrypt` ciphertext was not bound to the connection that produced it, so one user's blob could be handed to another user's session and decrypted. `encryptForOwner` / `decryptForOwner` add the owner as AES-GCM additional authenticated data under a `v2:` envelope.

- pre-binding blob → `400` "Value predates owner binding and must be re-entered"
- wrong owner → `403` "Value does not belong to this connection"

`app/providers.tsx` keeps the stored value on `403` rather than deleting it.

### Breaking: existing tokens and sessions do not survive the upgrade

`app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts` resolves a connection's `host`/`port`
from the connection URL before minting a PAT. Tokens minted before that carry
the `localhost` defaults instead — an identity *every* such token shares, and
the same identity the `v2:` ciphertext envelope binds blobs to. Honouring them
would let any pre-existing token act as, and decrypt for, that shared identity,
which is the hole this PR closes.

There is therefore no safe compatibility path: a `pbv` (PAT binding version)
claim is required on the JWT, and tokens without it are refused with `401`.
**Every PAT issued before this release stops working and must be reissued** from
Settings → Tokens, or via `POST /api/auth/tokens/credentials`.

The same reasoning applies to browser session cookies, which carry the binding
under `bv`: a session minted before this release records `localhost:6379` for a
URL login, and the URL itself was never stored, so there is nothing to repair it
from. The `jwt` callback retires those tokens, so **everyone signed in before the
upgrade is signed out once and has to log in again**; their query history, chats
and styles are unaffected. Deployments that ran the Docker image are signed out
regardless, since the baked `AUTH_SECRET` it used to verify those cookies with is
gone (below).

### Secrets

- The Dockerfile baked a fixed `AUTH_SECRET` into every image, making session tokens forgeable across deployments. Removed; `docker-entrypoint.sh` generates a random one when unset and now **exits** on a known placeholder rather than warning.
- The Helm chart generates-or-reuses its own secret and `fail`s on placeholders.
- `cleanup-auth` compared secrets with `===` (timing oracle, and `&&` short-circuited the multi-secret loop). Now hashes and uses `timingSafeEqual` across every configured secret.
- `docker-compose.minio.yml` images pinned by digest.

### UI

A long error toast grew past the viewport and took its dismiss button with it. The toast is capped at `60vh` and its body scrolls.

## Tests

- **`e2e/tests/cypherInjection.spec.ts`** (new) — hostile labels, relationship types, attribute keys and values are stored as data; read-only connections and read-only users are refused. **Negative-controlled**: reverting the label fix makes it fail by actually deleting a sentinel node.
- New owner-binding cases in `encryption.spec.ts`, a PAT-name injection case in `settingsTokens.spec.ts`, and a cap/scroll case in `errorToasts.spec.ts` (also negative-controlled).
- Unit tests for the AAD envelope, `looksServerEncrypted`, and the constant-time cleanup comparison.

Local: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 507/507 unit tests, eslint 0 errors on every touched file, and the affected Playwright specs green on `[Admin] Chromium`, `[Read-Write] - Chromium` and `[Read-Only] - Chromium`.

## Notes for reviewers

- `/api/encryption/encrypt` and `/api/encryption/decrypt` have no callers and no swagger entries. They are hardened here for consistency, but deleting them is a defensible alternative.
- The Helm changes could not be rendered locally (no `helm` installed) — CI's kind test is the real check.
- `.github/workflows/playwright.yml`'s smoke container now generates a random per-run secret, since the entrypoint refuses to start on a placeholder. The three remaining `NEXTAUTH_SECRET=SECRET` lines in that workflow run `npm start` directly and never reach the entrypoint.
- Not reachable from e2e: the Dockerfile/entrypoint `AUTH_SECRET` behaviour, the Helm chart, and the compose digests.

title: Add a configurable graph list order (newest first by default)
body:
The graph manager listed graphs in whatever order `GRAPH.LIST` returned. This adds a **Graphs Order** setting with four orders — `new-old` (default), `old-new`, `a-z`, `z-a` — applied to the graph selector, the Manage Graphs table and the graph-count tooltip.

`GRAPH.LIST` is answered by a keyspace scan, so it carries no creation time and no stable order. The chronological orders are therefore based on when this browser first saw each graph.

### `lib/graphSortOrder.ts` (new)
- Sort orders, their settings labels, and normalization of a stored value.
- First-seen timestamps per graph name, kept in connection-scoped storage (`graphsFirstSeen`) so two servers never share a history. Names that disappear are pruned, so a name reused after a drop counts as a new graph.
- `renameGraphFirstSeen` carries a renamed graph's timestamp over, so it keeps its place.
- Pure `sortGraphNames`, with a name tie-break for the chronological orders — every graph that already existed on the first load was seen in the same pass, so without it that list would be arbitrary.

```ts
// alpha and zebra were both seen on the first load; mango was created later
sortGraphNames(["zebra", "alpha", "mango"], "new-old", firstSeen)
// => ["mango", "alpha", "zebra"]
```

### Settings
- `graphsSortOrder` wired through `BrowserSettingsContext`, `localStorage` load/save/reset, and the draft/`hasChanges` plumbing, following the neighbouring Max Tabs setting.
- A select in Settings → Browser → User Experience: Newest First / Oldest First / Name (A-Z) / Name (Z-A).

### `app/graph/selectGraph.tsx`
- Records first-seen timestamps when the list arrives, and renders the sorted list. Recording is skipped while the list is still loading (so nothing is pruned) and while the tutorial is open (its demo graphs are not the user's).
- `setOptions` write-backs still use the unsorted list, so the periodic refresh keeps handing down the same array identity and doesn't rebuild every table row.

### Tests
`lib/graphSortOrder.test.ts` covers normalization, each order, the tie-break, recording/pruning, the rename, the unprefixed-storage guard and malformed stored data.

title: feat(mobile): responsive layout for viewports under 1100px
body:
## What

Makes the browser usable below ~1100px. Desktop is untouched: every change is either a `mobile:` Tailwind variant or an `isMobile` branch, with two deliberate exceptions called out below.

## Why

The UI assumed a desktop-sized window. Under ~1100px the header, toolbars and side panels ran out of room and overlapped each other, and a handful of actions were simply unreachable on a touch device because they were bound to right-click or to a modifier key a phone cannot press.

## Foundations

| | |
|---|---|
| `lib/useIsMobile.ts` | `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT = 1100`, plus `useViewportResolved()` so components can hold off until the width is known instead of flashing the wrong layout. |
| `mobile:` variant | `@custom-variant mobile (@media (width < 1100px))` in `app/globals.css` — one breakpoint that CSS and component logic agree on. |
| `components/ui/BottomSheet.tsx` | A sheet that stays mounted while closed (`translate-y-full` + `inert`). vaul's `Drawer` unmounts its children, which loses panel state on every dismiss. Its `push` variant shrinks the canvas instead of covering it. |
| `app/components/ui/HelpTip.tsx` | Popover on touch, tooltip on desktop. |

## Layout

- Graph chrome becomes a two-row toolbar, with the data, graph-info, chat and canvas-tools panels as bottom sheets. Zoom controls float above whichever sheet is open.
- Navigation, and the theme / settings / logout / support / About actions, move into a drawer behind a hamburger.
- Narrow-viewport passes over the dialogs, `TableComponent`/`PaginationList`, the Cypher editor, the query-history panel, Upload, Manage Graphs and all of `/settings`.

## Interaction changes

Two changes that are **not** mobile-only, because a touch device has no way to produce the gesture they replaced:

1. **Right-click is gone.** Left click selects, double click expands. Previously left click expanded and right click selected.
2. **Multi-select toggle** (mobile only) makes every tap additive — the stand-in for the Ctrl-click that Add Edge and bulk Delete require. While it is on, the data panel stays closed so it does not cover the elements still to be picked, a background tap no longer wipes the selection, and Delete is surfaced in the toolbar. It resets if the viewport widens past the breakpoint, so additive clicks can never outlive the toggle that turns them off.

Tooltips are the third gap: Radix tooltips never open on touch (they bail out of `onPointerMove` for `pointerType === "touch"`), so any hint that lived only in a `title` was invisible on a phone. `HelpTip` covers the load-bearing ones.

`About` also had no entry in the mobile menu at all — it is now in the drawer's help section, sharing its content with the desktop panel.

## Tests

- New `[Admin: Mobile] Chromium` Playwright project at 390×844 with `hasTouch`, driving `e2e/tests/mobile.spec.ts` (13 tests) through a `mobileGraphPage` page object. A narrow viewport rather than a device preset, because the layout is driven purely by width and `isMobile` emulation adds meta-viewport scaling that makes assertions less predictable.
- Wired into the sharded CI run; the desktop projects `testIgnore` the new spec.
- `canvas.spec.ts` gained coverage for the click/double-click model.

Locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 490 unit tests, `[Admin: Mobile]` 13/13, `canvas.spec.ts` 30/30, `graph.spec.ts` 17/17.

## Known gaps (follow-ups, not in this PR)

- The query-history panel still hints "Ctrl/Cmd + Left Click for multi select" and gates its row selection on `ctrlKey` — unreachable on touch. Wants per-row checkboxes.
- Several touch targets are still under 44px; the multi-select toggle is 31×31.
- Manage Graphs scrolls horizontally on a phone because of the Memory Usage column.
- Each additive tap still recentres the view.

Release notes

Sourced from react-hook-form's releases.

Version 7.87.0

✨ Features

  • Add shouldTouch option to trigger() ([#13671](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13671))

    setValue already supported shouldTouch; trigger() now does too. This allows you to mark field(s) as touched after manual or programmatic validation, such as validate-on-mount or multi-step form navigation, without needing a setValue workaround:

    // Mark a single field as touched after validating it
await trigger('firstName', { shouldTouch: true });

    // Mark every mounted field as touched after validating the whole form
await trigger(undefined, { shouldTouch: true });

  • Add OpaqueTypes registry for opaque leaf types ([#13676](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13676))

    Recursive type helpers (Path, DeepPartial, DeepRequired, FieldErrorsImpl, etc.) previously stopped only at Primitive | BrowserNativeObject. As a result, rich third-party value types such as Dayjs and Decimal could be recursively traversed member-by-member, potentially causing TypeScript to report "Excessive complexity" diagnostics on large form types.

    You can now register a type as an opaque leaf via declaration merging:

    import type { Dayjs } from 'dayjs';

    declare module 'react-hook-form' {
interface OpaqueTypes {
dayjs: Dayjs;
}
}

    While the registry is empty, types remain identical to the existing behavior. This is purely opt-in.

title: Add mTLS client-certificate authentication
body:
Adds optional **mTLS client-certificate authentication** for TLS connections, alongside the existing server-CA support.

### What it does
Threads a client `cert` and `key` (base64 PEM) through the same paths the existing `ca` field uses, and passes them to the Node TLS socket as single PEM strings. The login form gains two uploads, shown when TLS is enabled.

### Handling of the private key
The key is treated as a secret, not like the public CA:
- **Encrypted at rest** as `encrypted_key`, using the same `encrypt()`/`decrypt()` as the connection password (CA and cert stay plaintext — they are public).
- **Never placed in a JWT/PAT**, and not returned on the NextAuth `User`.
- **Server verification is untouched** — purely additive; `rejectUnauthorized` keeps its default and no skip/insecure path was added or widened.

### Scope
- **API tokens are password-based**: that route persists neither cert/key (nor ca/tls), so rather than issue a token that authenticates once and then fails on reconnect, it refuses cert/key explicitly.
- **Validation rejects half-configured mTLS** — a certificate without its key, or either with TLS disabled — by name, instead of failing later in the handshake.

`tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors.

_(Supersedes #2083, which I opened from the wrong account.)_

title: fix(chat): keep CYPHER keyword on parameter headers in displayed queries
body:
Fixes #2076

## Root cause

Not a `text-to-cypher` regression. The library (0.2.4 on staging) correctly normalizes LLM output to `CYPHER sourceCode='TLV' targetDesc='Narita' MATCH …` and executes it fine — the chat *answer* works.

The bug is in the Browser client: `app/graph/Chat.tsx` ran

```ts
data.cypherQuery.replace(/^cypher\s+/i, "")
```

on the returned query before displaying it. This was added (09bfe49a) to strip a leftover ```` ```cypher ```` fence-language tag, but it is too greedy and also removes the **mandatory** `CYPHER` keyword of a FalkorDB parameter header. The query shown in the chat bubble / ▶ Run / Copy therefore becomes `sourceCode='TLV' … MATCH …`, which fails with `Invalid input 'o': expected SET or START`. Confirmed present in the deployed staging bundle (`app/graph/page-*.js`).

## Fix

- New `app/graph/cypherDisplay.ts` → `stripCypherFenceTag()`: strips a leading `cypher` only when it is directly followed by a query clause keyword (fence residue); leaves `CYPHER name='x' MATCH …` untouched.
- `Chat.tsx` uses the helper.
- Unit tests (`cypherDisplay.test.ts`) incl. the exact query from the issue screenshot.

## Verification

- `node --test`: 4/4 pass; `tsc` + `eslint` clean.
- Native binding test: fed the screenshot's bare-param query through `@falkordb/text-to-cypher` 0.2.4 → normalized + executed (`status: success`). Same input on 0.2.3 (Browser 2.3.1) reproduces the issue error, so 2.3.1 additionally needs the already-shipped dependency bump.
- **Real UI (Playwright, local FalkorDB + airports dataset, mock LLM returning the screenshot's malformed query):**
  - before fix: chat shows `sourceCode='TLV' …`, ▶ Run sends the invalid query.
  - after fix: chat shows `CYPHER sourceCode='TLV' …`, ▶ Run executes and returns the path (`codes: [TLV, IST, NRT]`, `pathWeight: 2`).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved display of generated Cypher queries by removing stray code-block language markers when appropriate.
  * Preserved valid Cypher parameter headers and queries without removable markers.
  * Ensured queries with valid `CYPHER` parameter headers remain intact when displayed and executed from chat.
  * Improved reliability when running generated queries with parameters, preventing malformed queries and related errors.

title: Improve UDF library panel expansion and function-to-code navigation
body:
This change improves UDF browsing UX by making library expansion content-first and wiring function clicks directly to the corresponding location in the library source viewer. Expanded library context is now prioritized in the panel, and function discovery is actionable.

  - Track expansion at panel level so the most recently expanded library is treated as the active expanded section.

  - Load/select library source when expanding a library, so the right pane reflects the active library immediately.

- **Function click → editor navigation**
  - Convert function rows from static text to interactive controls.
  - Add `selectedUdfFunction` to UDF context state to carry function-intent from sidebar to editor view.
  - On function click, ensure the library is selected, then trigger navigation intent for that function.

- **Editor-side function location**
  - Capture Monaco editor instance and react to function selection intent.
  - Introduce a focused locator utility (`findFunctionLine`) to resolve function names to line numbers across common declaration forms:
    - `function name(...)`
    - `const name = (...) => ...`
    - `name: function (...) ...`
  - Center/reveal the resolved line in the main file viewer.

- **Navigation utility (new)**
  - Added a small dedicated helper plus tests for line resolution behavior:
    - `app/udf/functionNavigation.ts`
    - `app/udf/functionNavigation.test.ts`

```ts
const lineNumber = findFunctionLine(selectedUdf[5], selectedUdfFunction);
if (lineNumber) {
```

title: fix: address AI review findings on relationship styling
body:
Follow-up to #2021, which merged while its AI review threads were still open. Each finding below was re-verified against the merged code; only the still-valid ones are changed here.

## Fixed

| Finding | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Save during the tutorial left the preview applied for the rest of the session | `handleSave` now reverts before closing when `tutorialOpen` — the tutorial runs on a demo graph and never persisted the style anyway |
| `handleClose` comment claimed it did *not* revert, while the code does | Comment corrected |
| Relationship **Customize** reused `customizeStyle<name>`, colliding with the node label button (and with the tutorial's `customizeStylePerson`) | Relationship button is now `customizeRelationshipStyle<name>` |
| Tutorial step "Get KNOWS edge" only opened the new popover — it no longer ran the query, and did not forward `pointerdown` so the popover could not open through the overlay | Split into "Open Edge Options" (forwards `pointerdown`) + "Get KNOWS edge" on `runRelationshipKNOWS`, mirroring the existing two-step node label flow. Resume-track `startIndex` values shifted for the inserted step |
| `SCOPED_KEY_PREFIXES` doc comment only described the `prefix-graphName` shape | Comment now covers `labelStyle_<label>` too |
| No coverage for `convertToCanvasData` forwarding the link style dimensions | Two cases added to `lib/utils.test.ts` |

## Not changed, with reasons

- **"`width` / `fontSize` / `arrowSize` can be `undefined`, default them to the canvas constants"** — `@falkordb/canvas@0.2.6` already does exactly that: `link.width ?? LINK_WIDTH`, `link.fontSize ?? LINK_FONT_SIZE`, `link.arrowSize ?? ARROW_SIZE`. Node `size` relies on the same undefined-is-default contract. Duplicating the defaults here would pin them to whatever the constants were at write time. The new unit test locks the `undefined` passthrough in.
- **"Cancel/Close does not restore relationship text metrics"** — `textWidth` / `textHeight` / `textAscent` / `textDescent` are vestigial fields on `Label` / `Relationship`: nothing in the app reads or writes them. The `falkordb-browser` Helm chart could not be retargeted to mirrored/private registries without rewriting the full image repository string, and it did not honor `global.imageRegistry` when used as a subchart.
